A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a series of behavioral interventions that have been tested in cancer survivors and have been found to improve dietary intake of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, fiber, calcium, and vitamin D and to decrease intake of fat, saturated fat, sodium, and refined grains.

nutrition education and guidance by a registered dietitian should be a part of the care team throughout the cancer continuum and that lifestyle intervention should be tailored to the needs of the individual patient.

patients and survivors need to be educated on the importance of eating well and the benefits to their health and well-being.
cancer patients and survivors can be empowered to improve their diet and nutrition by using evidence-based behavioral strategies that are designed to be practical and sustainable in the long-term.
